title: A full fleet still moved the rotation cursor to the read's last project, so backlogs drained first in, first out
resolution: A decline for lack of fleet capacity (quarantine, worker eligibility or capacity, no candidate) no longer counts as an offer; with nothing placed the cursor stops before the first one; contract, spec, and design state it.

title: The outage test passed with the cursor left unmoved or the failed offer counted, because the first project had no task left
resolution: Added a later task of the first project to the outage test and a test of an outage at the first offer with a cursor set; both fail on temporary mutants of those two defects.

title: The no-candidate test started without a cursor, so resetting the cursor would pass
resolution: The test now sets the cursor with a placing pass before the pass without a candidate; it fails on a mutant that resets the cursor.

title: The pass runner discarded each pass result, so an unexpected failure went unnoticed
resolution: runPass checks every pass result: ok for the normal passes, a failure for the expected outage.

title: The offer loop mutated a cursor passed in and also answered the placement count
resolution: #offer(order, after) builds the cursor and returns the count or the outage with the next cursor; #placeDue stores it.

title: Contract section 5 said the rotation starts after the project that last received capacity, untrue after a pass that placed nothing
resolution: Section 5 now says the rotation starts after the rotation cursor that item 18 fixes.

title: The placement queue port comment still said the caller passes the last project read
resolution: The comment now says that passing the rotation cursor reaches P blocked projects in ceil(P/limit) reads.

title: The rotation requirement did not say that an offer the store failed does not count
resolution: The requirement now says an offer the store failed does not count.
